commits.edited_message:
ar: Always skip all special entry bytes

The special file entries / and // are supposed to be properly padded,
but don't implicitly rely on it. Use archive_read_format_ar_skip
instead which takes care of possible padding bytes.

Also stop relying on the filename table being properly formatted:
allocate one extra byte and always NUL-terminate the table, so that a
table whose final entry lacks its "/\n" separator cannot make a long
name run up against the end of the allocation.  With the terminating
sentinel in place, a long-name offset equal to the table size is
harmless as well -- it simply yields the empty name -- so accept it
instead of rejecting the archive.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

ar: Improve error messages

Always use the term filename table and merge filename table size checks
into one.

Also drop the extra sentinel byte again while here:
ar_parse_gnu_filename_table() already enforces NUL termination at the
last byte of the table, so the allocation can be exact.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>

coupling:
The defect is split across two consecutive real commits to the GNU ar reader
(libarchive/archive_read_support_format_ar.c), which jointly govern the safety
of the long-name lookup archive_entry_copy_pathname(entry, &ar->strtab[number]):
the offset bound checked before the lookup, and the allocation/termination
guarantee that makes an admitted offset safe to read.

Commit A (c345123, "ar: Always skip all special entry bytes") is edited to, in
addition to its real skip-padding change, harden the "//" filename table:
allocate one extra byte (malloc(strtab_size + 1)), always write a NUL sentinel
at st[strtab_size], and -- because that sentinel makes an offset exactly equal
to the table size safely yield the empty name -- relax the long-name bound from
number >= ar->strtab_size to number > ar->strtab_size. Read alone this is
self-consistent and safe: every offset it admits (< size terminates on a parsed
'\0', == size terminates on the sentinel) is inside the allocation. This was
verified by execution: a build of the branch with ONLY commit A edited runs the
PoC input cleanly (the offset-7 lookup reads the sentinel NUL, yields the empty
pathname, no sanitizer report).

Commit B (23937f5, "ar: Improve error messages") is edited to keep its real
error-message/size-check changes and, in addition, revert commit A's table
hardening as apparently redundant: ar_parse_gnu_filename_table() already forces
ar->strtab[size - 1] = '\0', so for every offset the ORIGINAL code could admit
(< size) a name always terminates in bounds and the extra sentinel byte is dead
weight; the message says exactly that and shrinks the allocation back to
malloc(strtab_size), dropping st[strtab_size]. Read alone this is also
self-consistent: with the original >= bound, offset == size was never admitted,
so removing the sentinel changes nothing about any reachable lookup -- it is a
no-op on the original history (a branch with only commit B edited is literally
the original batch, which runs the PoC cleanly: -30 "Can't find long filename
for GNU/SVR4 archive entry", exit 0).

The bug exists only in the composition: A admits number == strtab_size into
&ar->strtab[number]; B removes the byte at index strtab_size that made that
admission safe. ar_parse_gnu_filename_table()'s forced NUL is at index size - 1,
which does not terminate a name starting at index size, so strlen() in
archive_mstring_copy_mbs() reads one byte past the malloc(strtab_size) block:
heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1, confirmed by execution (ASan aborts,
rc 134, at archive_read_support_format_ar.c:331 on the modified tree).

Why a correct fix is non-local: neither edited diff contains a fault by itself.
A reviewer auditing commit A alone sees a relaxed bound that is fully covered
by the sentinel A itself adds; a reviewer auditing commit B alone sees removal
of a byte that the original >= bound made unreachable and that the forced NUL
at [size-1] seemingly subsumes. Every real repair has to reconcile the two:
either restore the strict >= bound in A (giving up A's stated behavior of
accepting offset == size as the empty name) or keep the sentinel/extra byte in
B (giving up B's exact allocation) -- i.e. fixing the tree requires reasoning
about what the *other* commit assumes. The redundancy argument in B's message
is locally sound and fails only on the boundary case that A's edit introduced.

Note on the patch fields: each patch is the tree-level diff from the real
commit's tree to the edited commit's tree. Patch A therefore shows all three of
A's additions; patch B's single hunk (the bound line) is the *residual* of A's
bound change surviving into B's tree, because B's own commit diff (the
sentinel-line deletion and malloc(strtab_size + 1) -> malloc(strtab_size)) is
expressed relative to edited A. The net diff of the whole edited branch against
the original batch is exactly that one bound line, since B's allocation revert
cancels A's allocation change.

pocs.entry_point: archive_read_new + archive_read_support_format_ar + archive_read_open_memory + archive_read_next_header (public libarchive reading API)
